title: affordance-tiler: declarative budgeted batch templates + quantization fence CLI
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a new 'affordance-tiler' CLI that generates budget-aware batch templates and a conservative quantization fence; no behavioral changes to existing APIs. Intended as opt-in defaults and tooling for tenant onboarding.
description:
Motivation: Customers frequently ask for a way to codify budget/latency tradeoffs as shareable templates and to prevent overly aggressive quantization during automated rollouts. This PR introduces 'affordance-tiler', a small declarative templates-as-code subsystem plus a CLI previewer and a conservative quantization 'fence' that blocks quant profiles which historically increased perplexity by >X% in our evals.

What this PR does (single-line description followed by details):
- Adds a templates module that compiles tenant budget/latency constraints into batch/cache/quant suggestion bundles (JSON templates that can be applied via rwctl or the infra API).
- Provides rwctl affordance-tiler preview and dry-run commands so SRE/SEs can inspect expected unit-econ delta before applying.
- Introduces a quant_fence that hooks into the autosuggest pipeline: quant profiles flagged by the fence are listed as "blocked" and require manual approval. The fence is conservative by default and driven by threshold JSON shipped with the telemetry templates.
- Ships telemetry templates (telemetry/templates/budgeted_batch.json) that add unit-econ counters and delta histograms used by the Optimize team.
- Includes docs and examples for onboarding and a short e2e integration test for the CLI.

Why unique: Instead of pushing a single default, the affordance-tiler encourages templated tradeoffs (e.g., "latency-tier: moderate + budget: low") and provides a human-in-the-loop safety net for quantization that reduced past regressions. This is intended to be used together with the existing econ-suggester but as an opt-in policy layer for tenants.

Checklist:
- [x] Templates compiler + representation (pkg/econ/templates)
- [x] rwctl subcommand and dry-run preview (cmd/rwctl/affordance_tiler.go)
- [x] Quant fence implementation and config loader (pkg/econ/quant_fence.go)
- [x] Telemetry templates and example dashboards (telemetry/templates/budgeted_batch.json, docs/telemetry.md)
- [x] Integration test for preview and template apply (tests/integration/tiler_cli_test.go)
- [x] Docs and quickstart (docs/affordance-tiler.md)

Diff summary (high-level, not a full patch):
- New: pkg/econ/templates/tiler.go - template compiler and serializer (core logic + unit tests).
- New: pkg/econ/quant_fence.go - fence logic, threshold loader and API surface used by suggester.
- New: cmd/rwctl/affordance_tiler.go - CLI commands: preview, dry-run, apply (apply is gated behind an experiment flag).
- New: telemetry/templates/budgeted_batch.json - telemetry schema for unit-econ counters and delta histograms.
- New: docs/affordance-tiler.md - onboarding guide and examples.
- New: tests/integration/tiler_cli_test.go - integration test that runs preview and validates expected JSON output.

Commits (summary):
- feat(tiler): initial compiler and template model
- feat(cli): add rwctl affordance-tiler preview/dry-run commands
- feat(quant): quant_fence implementation and config loader
- docs: onboarding guide and telemetry examples
- tests: add integration test for CLI preview

Testing and CI notes:
- First CI run failed on unit test related to a flakey histogram helper (pkg/telemetry/hist_test.go). I fixed the helper and force-pushed.
- Second CI run passed all checks (build, unit, integration, lint). The PR was approved by Jonah and Priya after one round of feedback on error messages and logging verbosity.

Rollout plan:
- Merge to main behind feature flag (affordance_tiler_enabled=false).
- Run canary with 2 pilot tenants (internal staging tenants) and collect econ deltas for 48h.
- If deltas are within expected bounds and no regressions in NLU eval sets, flip feature flag and enable opt-in defaults in Console.

Backwards compatibility and safety:
- All changes are behind opt-in paths: templates are not applied automatically. The quant_fence returns metadata but does not mutate existing profiles.
- Telemetry schemas are additive.
